title: Female borrowers who include explicit thanks to lenders may fund faster.
Providing specific demographic details about children, such as number and schooling status, predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who describe having fewer children may fund faster.
Female borrowers who explain the microfinance program's role or collateral constraints may fund faster.
Male borrowers who mention external financial obligations or organizational memberships may fund more slowly.
Pitches from both men and women that explicitly reference a successful track record of repaying previous loans tend to accelerate funding speed.
Male borrowers who explicitly mention a desire to increase sales or income may fund faster.
Female borrowers who write significantly longer pitches may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention a specific city or province may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention working together with a husband may fund faster.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention benefits to their family or community fund faster.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that provide concrete financial figures or specific inventory lists fund faster regardless of gender.
Mentioning family obligations and benefits has opposite effects on funding speed by gender.
Mentioning local currency amounts or specific institutional affiliations predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who explicitly state their own age in the pitch fund more slowly.
